description.narrative: The restructured Social Protection Transformation Project (SPTP) aims to strengthen Rwanda's shift toward job-focused social protection outcomes. Component 2 of the parent project will become component 1 in the restructured project and will receive increased financing to intensify and scale economic inclusion interventions, through an enhanced graduation package—climate-sensitive public works, skills development, linkage to job opportunities in selected sectors, seed capital, and mentoring—targeting microenterprise development in high job-potential sectors such as agriculture, environmental protection, infrastructure and construction. These efforts will leverage existing local economic development initiatives, World Bank agriculture operations, and partnerships with relevant ministries such as the Ministry of Agriculture. Professionalization of the community workforce, caregivers and para-social workers will be further enhanced to improve service quality and effectively support vulnerable households on graduation pathways, through mentorship and resilient livelihood activities, and to enhance their prospects for formal employment and strengthen the long-term resilience of their own households. Component 1 of the parent project will become component 2 in the restructured project. The component will enhance human capital investments while improving the resilience of households with limited labor capacity. It focuses on three key activities namely (i) investment in HB-ECD centers and caregiver public works; (ii) Smart Start support for pregnant and lactating women and children in their first 1,000 days through flexible public works, healthcare and nutrition services, and behavioral change interventions; and (iii) basic needs support for households with limited labor capacity, including those with persons with disabilities, child headed households and the elderly. Professionalization and certification of ECD caregivers will help sustain HB-ECD service delivery and enhance nutrition and learning outcomes outcomes for children, whilst improving women's employment potential.Components 3 and 4 of the parent project will be consolidated to form component 3 of the restructured project. The objective is to streamline delivery systems, capacity building, coordination, behavior change communication and M&E for downstream delivery across decentralized levels. With core systems, such as the social registry and digital payments already functional, future work will focus on system maintenance, integration, and application to other programs, including health insurance subsidies for vulnerable groups.
To increase the number of poor and vulnerable people who benefit from new or better jobs, expand their access to human capital services, and strengthen social protection delivery systems.
